bullets.title: The Glorious, Almost-Disconnected Boredom of My Walk in Japan
bullets.creator: Craig Mod
bullets.note:
convertkit-mail.com/c/92unw45ooanhpzn8gsg/l8fehmhnpx0g5n/aHR0cHM6Ly90d2l0dGVyLmNvbS9jcmFpZ21vZA==)**), from** **_WIRED_****.** I printed this out weeks ago and placed it on my kitchen table to read. Each time I walked past it, I had the distinct feeling of “this seems important for me to read,” and it was. This article is a beautiful and highly tactical description of long walks, using technology on your terms, and finding stillness. Here are two paragraphs out of many that I loved:  
  
_I have configured servers, written code, built web pages, helped design products used by millions of people. I am firmly in the camp that believes technology is generally bending the world in a positive direction. Yet, for me, Twitter foments neurosis, Facebook sadness, Google News a sense of foreboding. Instagram turns me covetous. All of them make me want to do it—whatever “it” may be—for the likes, the comments. I can’t help but feel that I am the worst version of myself, being performative on a very short, very depressing timeline. A timeline of seconds.  
__...  
__In the context of a walk like this, “boredom” is a goal, the antipode of mindless connectivity, constant stimulation, anger and dissatisfaction. I put “boredom” in quotes because the boredom I’m talking about fosters a heightened sense of presence. To be “bored” is to be free of distraction._

bullets.title: Spirited Away in Minecraft Tour
bullets.note: This is a nerd double whammy. _Spirited Away_ is my all-time favorite movie, but it’s historically been hard to find on streaming services. This video scratches the itch and showcases two things: (1) the bathhouse of the gods (and much more) from the movie, and (2) the absolutely mind-numbing amount of work required to recreate it at this level of detail in Minecraft. [Alan Becker](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/92unw45ooanhpzn8gsg/70c7h8h6enkgvp/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vY2hhbm5lbC9VQ3JIUm9PenJNUmw2OHVUeUJpZDl2bHc=), you’re an animal. Alan has created many other [Studio Ghibli](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/92unw45ooanhpzn8gsg/zrsghnhkzl4g98/aHR0cHM6Ly9lbi53aWtpcGVkaWEub3JnL3dpa2kvU3R1ZGlvX0doaWJsaQ==) fantasyscapes [here](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/92unw45ooanhpzn8gsg/z5aghnhkzl4g9r/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vY2hhbm5lbC9VQ3JIUm9PenJNUmw2OHVUeUJpZDl2bHc=).

bullets.section: Supplement I’m experimenting with for cycling training —
bullets.title: HumanN BeetElite Concentrated Beet Powder
bullets.note: This is used by a number of ultra-endurance athletes I know, and, possible placebo effect aside, it seems to help with longer-duration rides. bullets.section: Quote I’m pondering, not totally buying, but finding useful for introspection —
bullets.title: “Anytime you're practicing renunciation, you're deluded. How about that! You're deluded. What are you renouncing? Anytime you renounce something, you are tied forever to the thing you renounce. There's a guru in India who says, ‘Every time a prostitute comes to me, she's talking about nothing but God. She says I'm sick of this life that I'm living. I want God. But every time a priest comes to me, he's talking about nothing but sex.’ Very well, when you renounce something, you're stuck to it forever. When you fight something, you're tied to it forever. As long as you're fighting it, you are giving it power. You give it as much power as you are using to fight it.”— Anthony de Mello, Awareness And, as always, please give me feedback on Twitter.
